desc: Ask [C17]: What are my design intentions for the browser extension?

body.question: What are my design intentions for the browser extension?

response:
{"id":20,"answer":"From your saved notes, your design intentions for packaging the app as a browser extension are a sketch rather than a full spec — these are the concrete points recorded:

• Extension as the eventual form factor — the website/app "will be made into an extension later, for this application" (note 2).
• Core capture behavior — the extension "captures the active tab text and pushes it to DeepNotes with the URL" (note 13).
• Context tracking by default — "the system will be tracking all kinds of data of the user by default," and those contexts are meant to be used "to better organize the info" (note 2).
• Privacy counterweight — you flagged that this tracking-by-default idea "needs a privacy toggle" (note 13).
• Product framing behind it — a local-first notes app that organizes itself in the background, where "notes stay untouched; an interpretation layer evolves," with privacy as a likely point to surface publicly (note 6).

Adjacent thought worth noting: you saved the Stafford Beer line "the purpose of a system is what it does" explicitly as a counter to design intentions (note 26) — i.e., a reminder to judge the extension by observed behavior, not stated plans.

Not recorded in your notes: any decision about extension architecture (manifest version, storage/sync path, permissions model), what specifically counts as "context" being tracked, where the privacy toggle would live or what it would gate, and how the extension would interact with the existing local-first store. Your retrieval decision (lexical + graph now, embeddings deferred to v2) is about search, not the extension. So treat the above as intent, not settled design.
